steps.message:
﻿# Fix Maven Compilation Failure: logback-classic 1.2.11 -> 1.4.1

## Context

Project `pay-adminusers` (by alphagov) has a **COMPILATION_FAILURE** after a dependency upgrade bot bumped
`ch.qos.logback:logback-classic` from `1.2.11` to `1.4.1` (minor update).

Reference PR: https://github.com/alphagov/pay-adminusers/pull/1594

## Your Task

The source code is in `/pay-adminusers`. Fix all compilation errors so that `mvn compile` succeeds.
I'll start by running `mvn compile` to see the actual compilation errors, then fix them.

arguments.description: Run maven compile to see errors

steps.message:
I found the issue! There are conflicting logback versions:
- `logback-classic:1.4.1` (explicitly declared)
- `logback-core:1.2.11` and `logback-access:1.2.11` (transitive from Dropwizard)

Logback 1.4.x requires all logback modules to have the same version. Let me verify this is causing the compilation issue and then fix it:

Found the compilation error:
```
cannot access org.slf4j.spi.LoggingEventAware
  class file for org.slf4j.spi.LoggingEventAware not found
```

The issue is that **Logback 1.4.x requires SLF4J 2.x**, but the project uses SLF4J 1.7.36. The `LoggingEventAware` interface was added in SLF4J 2.x.

The fix is to upgrade `slf4j-api` to version 2.x. Let me update the pom.xml:

Logback 1.4.x requires SLF4J 2.x, but the project had:
- `logback-classic:1.4.1` (upgraded by bot)
- `slf4j-api:1.7.36` (old version)
- Transitive `logback-core:1.2.11` and `logback-access:1.2.11` from Dropwizard

This caused compilation error: `cannot access org.slf4j.spi.LoggingEventAware`

## Solution (pom.xml changes)

1. **Upgraded SLF4J** from `1.7.36` to `2.0.3` (required by logback 1.4.x)

2. **Added explicit logback-core dependency** at version `1.4.1` to match logback-classic

3. **Excluded old logback artifacts** from Dropwizard dependencies:
   - `dropwizard-core`: excluded `logback-classic`, `logback-core`, `logback-access`
   - `dropwizard-json-logging`: excluded `logback-access`

The `mvn compile` command now succeeds.
